method_notes: ch3 single numbering 1-36, sections A-I = s1-s9. Section C (q11-15) 'chronological order': answer side renumbers the 5 events into chronological sequence; each key names its event -> paired by named event (flag on q11). Section D q16 and q12/q13 analogy etc.

Section A keys are TEXT-ONLY (no option letter): q1 'May 17, 1498', q2 '1602 AD', q3 'Queen Elizabeth', q4 'French', q5 'Francisco de Almeida'. Two-pass normalised match resolves q4(D French)/q5(A Almeida); q1/q2/q3 do not match an option verbatim (phrasing differs) -> 'key text not among options' review-blocking (builder auto; extraction does not force-match).
Section-header difficulty: C and D print '(Difficult)' with no per-question tag -> difficulty_source section_header (control rev 3).
Section B header prints '(1 mark)' -> marks flag text records it; marks left null (assigning marks is a procedure change, not extraction's).
q36 (section I) references a PRINTED MAP on the question page (pdf31) -> question-side stimulus (schema 1.7), attached as stimuli[] by the post-step; answer is the trading-centres list.
2 LO rows (09 main; 02 map-skills applies to q36). marks not printed except section B note. difficulty per-question tags win.

questions.text: Write about the trading centers of the Dutch in India?
questions.text_as_printed: Write about the trading centers of the Dutch in India? (Difficult )

answer.value:
Dutch trading centers:
The Dutch were one of the major European powers to arrive in India after the Portuguese.
They established the Dutch East India Company in 1602 and monopolized trade with the East.
They established their capital at Pulicat and set up trading centers in various parts of India, including Agra, Machilipatnam, Surat, Karaikal, Nagapattinam, and Kochi.

questions.text: How did the British East India Company transform from a simple trading firm in 1600 into a political power that ruled India?
questions.text_as_printed: How did the British East India Company transform from a simple trading firm in 1600 into a political power that ruled India? (Difficult )

answer.value:
East India Company:
The East India Company was a British private company established in 1600 to trade with the East.
Queen Elizabeth granted the company permission to trade in India.
The company's ships docked at the port of Surat.
Thomas Roe visited the court of Jahangir and obtained permission to trade in Surat.
The company established trading centers in Agra, Broach, and other parts of India.
The company's profits increased, and they obtained dastaks (documents granting exemption from customs duties) from Farrukhsiyar.
The British built fortifications for protection and maintained a strong military presence.

questions.text: How did their focus on controlling the profitable spice monopoly in Southeast Asia shape their trade operations in India?
questions.text_as_printed: How did their focus on controlling the profitable spice monopoly in Southeast Asia shape their trade operations in India? (Difficult )

answer.value:
Dutch East India Company:
The Dutch East India Company was established in 1602 and gained a monopoly over trade in India.
Their capital was at Pulicat, and they established trading centers in Agra, Machilipatnam, Surat, Karaikal, Nagapattinam, and Kochi.
Due to competition from the English, the Dutch focused on the Southeast Asian islands.
